entries.dictionary: 精選版 日本国語大辞典; 普及版 字通
entries.heading: ぎ【儀】; 儀 / 常用漢字 15画 / 字音 ギ
entries.evidence: Nikkoku distinguishes ceremonial conduct, appearance and a matter/affair, with a suffix used for oneself or one's side in formal notices and older correspondence. Jitsu supplies ギ and identifies 義 as the phonetic component.
entries.decision: Centre useful teaching on ceremony/formal conduct, with a bounded matter/case and formal-suffix qualification. Preserve sole sourced ギ and no kun readings. Jitsu's semantic 字訓 and historical glosses do not add modern metadata readings. Prefer a labelled modern-shape mnemonic; no historical derivation is needed.
entries.limits: Daijisen returned attribution only. Ancient forms and some compound spellings are gaiji images, not inspected glyphs. Do not claim to have verified those images or the detailed sacrificial history. The supplied phonetic observation is distinct from an explanation of the character's entire historical origin.

entries.dictionary: 精選版 日本国語大辞典; 普及版 字通
entries.heading: ぎ‐しき【儀式】; 【儀式】ぎしよく・ぎしき
entries.evidence: Nikkoku distinguishes formal rules/conduct and ceremonial procedures or the events themselves. Jitsu's short entry identifies a ceremony and includes another dictionary reading. The frozen JMdict family records the selected modern ぎしき ceremony/rite/ritual/service sense.
entries.decision: Reuse actual 儀式 ぎしき, N2, without changing its primary reading, identity, sense or exclusions. Its English service gloss is ceremonial, not every customer service. Add component navigation only. Do not introduce the other dictionary reading as an unrestricted substitute.
entries.limits: Daijisen and Nipponica returned attribution only. A separately named novel and historical court-ritual books are not the selected lexical identity. Historical dictionary coverage does not require adding those senses to the practical card.

entries.dictionary: 精選版 日本国語大辞典
entries.heading: れい‐ぎ【礼儀・礼義】
entries.evidence: The first sense concerns socially appropriate conduct and respectful manners; a separately illustrated historical sense is remuneration. Frozen JMdict gives manners/courtesy/etiquette and marks 礼義 as search-only.
entries.decision: Reuse actual 礼儀 れいぎ, N3, in its existing etiquette sense. Preserve its direct 行儀 exclusion. Do not turn the historical remuneration sense or the search-only spelling into a new support article or an ordinary substitute.
entries.limits: Daijisen, Jitsu and the new encyclopedia returned attribution only. The older encyclopedia excerpt is contextual discussion, not independent evidence for every usage claim. No universal cultural-conduct rule or frequency ranking is inferred.

entries.dictionary: 精選版 日本国語大辞典
entries.heading: ぎょう‐ぎギャウ‥【行儀・行義・形儀】
entries.evidence: The entry distinguishes conduct, standards of conduct and historical senses. The frozen JMdict family selects manners/behavior; related complete families separately record behaving well and bad manners.
entries.decision: Reuse actual 行儀 ぎょうぎ, N3, retaining evaluation by いい/悪い rather than translating the noun itself as inherently good. Add only its missing 儀 link and the 行 counterpart backlink.
entries.limits: Daijisen returned attribution only. Historical spellings and historical suru or adjectival uses are not unrestricted present-day alternatives to the selected practical noun sense.

entries.dictionary: 精選版 日本国語大辞典; 日本大百科全書; 改訂新版 世界大百科事典
entries.heading: ちきゅう‐ぎチキウ‥【地球儀】; 地球儀 ちきゅうぎ
entries.evidence: The actual definitions describe a three-dimensional model of the Earth. Complete frozen JMdict also supplies celestial/lunar globes and several measuring or astronomical instruments with final ぎ.
entries.decision: A concise kana-supplied 地球儀 ちきゅうぎ example can prevent an every-compound-means-ceremony shortcut. No new article is necessary for the sole ギ practice key. Do not label every 儀 compound a measuring instrument or force ceremony into globe vocabulary.
entries.limits: Daijisen returned attribution only. Encyclopedic historical chronology is not adopted; the two encyclopedias give different accounts of early Japanese transmission. Definitions, not historical reconstruction, support this bounded distinction.

failedLookups.disposition: Preserve the failed lookup; do not cite it as a verified public entry. Complete frozen JMdict 1002030 and 1733730 support the exact existing お辞儀 おじぎ and its base 辞儀. No replacement source was needed for a link-only reuse.
